# Leases %>%

industry_list <- unique(Leases$internal_industry)
market_list <- unique(Leases$market)

summary(Leases$leasedSF)

BigLeases <- subset(Leases, leasedSF >= 10000) 

FrequencyTimeSeries <- function(data) {   
  time <- ts(numeric(84), frequency=12, start=c(2018, 1))  
  for (i in 1:nrow(data)) {     
    seriesval <-(as.numeric(data[i,1])-2018)*12 + as.numeric(data[i, 3])     
    time[seriesval] <- time[seriesval]+1 }  
  return (time) }

#a line plot of big leases Time Series
BigLeasesTime <- FrequencyTimeSeries(subset(Leases,leasedSF >= 10000))
plot(BigLeasesTime)

AreaTimeSeries <- function(data) {   
  time <- ts(numeric(84), frequency=12, start=c(2018, 1))   
  for (i in 1:nrow(data)) {     
    seriesval <- (as.numeric(data[i,1])-2018)*12 + as.numeric(data[i, 3])     
    time[seriesval] <- time[seriesval]+data[i,14]/100000 }  
  return (time) }
#a line plot of Atlanta Area Time Series
plot(AreaTimeSeries(BigLeases))


# line plots of all 29 areas Time Series
for (area in market_list) {
  plot(FrequencyTimeSeries(subset(BigLeases, market == area)), 
       main= "Leases of area over 10000", sub=area, ylab="Frequency")
}












library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
Leases$overall_rent %>% group_by(year,quater)

rent <- Leases[c("year","quarter","monthsigned","market","overall_rent")]
rent <- rent[!duplicated(rent), ]

quarter_rent <- aggregate(rent$overall_rent, list(rent$year,rent$quarter,rent$market), FUN=mean)
colnames(quarter_rent) = c("year","quarter","market", "overall_rent")
quarter_rent <- na.omit(quarter_rent)
unique(quarter_rent$market)

quarter_rent <- quarter_rent %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(paste(year, 
                             match(quarter, c("Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4")) * 3 - 2, 
                             "01"), 
                       format = "%Y %m %d")) %>%
  filter(market %in% c("Manhattan","San Francisco",
                       "Los Angeles","Atlanta", "Detroit","Austin",
                       "Salt Lake City"))


# Line plot showing rent trends over time

  ggplot(quarter_rent, aes(x = date, y = overall_rent, color = market)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Atlanta" = "orange", "San Francisco" = "blue",
                                "Manhattan" = "lightblue",
                                "Los Angeles" = "#FF62BC88", 
                                "Detroit"="#00BF7D88","Austin"="#E73BF388",
                       "Salt Lake City"="#A3A50088")) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(title = "Quarterly Rent Trends (2018-2024)",
       x = "Year",
       y = "Overall Rent ($/SF)",
       color = "Market") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 18, face = "bold"),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_text(size=14), 
        legend.text = element_text(size=14)) + 
    geom_vline(xintercept = 2020-03-11, color="red", size=5)

ggsave("rent_trend.png")

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
SF <- subset(quarter_rent, rent$market == "San Francisco")

ggplot(SF, aes(y = overall_rent, x = date)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm') +
  labs(title = "San Francisco Rent")+
  theme_minimal()

NY <- subset(quarter_rent, rent$market == "Manhattan")

ggplot(SF, aes(y = overall_rent, x = date)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm') +
  labs(title = "Manhattan Rent")+
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r us map}
library(ggplot2)
library(maps)
library(ggrepel) # For better label placement

# Create a data frame with the cities and their coordinates
cities <- data.frame(
  city = c("Manhattan", "San Francisco", "Los Angeles", 
           "Atlanta", "Detroit", "Austin", "Salt Lake City"),
  lat = c(40.7831, 37.7749, 34.0522, 
          33.7490, 42.3314, 30.2672, 40.7608),
  lon = c(-73.9712, -122.4194, -118.2437, 
          -84.3880, -83.0458, -97.7431, -111.8910)
)

# Get US map data
us_map <- map_data("state")

# Plot the map with highlighted cities
ggplot() +
  # Draw the US map
  geom_polygon(data = us_map, 
               aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
               fill = "lightgray", color = "white") +
  
  # Add city points
  geom_point(data = cities, 
             aes(x = lon, y = lat), 
             color = "red", size = 3) +
  
  # Add city labels with repelling to avoid overlap
  geom_label_repel(data = cities, 
                  aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = city),
                  box.padding = 0.5, point.padding = 0.5,
                  segment.color = 'grey50') +
  
  # Adjust the coordinate system
  coord_map(xlim = c(-125, -65), ylim = c(25, 50)) +
  
  # Add titles and theme
  #labs(title = "Selected US Cities Highlighted on Map",
  #     caption = "Red dots indicate city locations") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 14),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10))


```
